```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE)
invisible(Sys.setlocale("LC_CTYPE", "C.UTF-8"))
library(data.table)
library(DT)
A <- "docs/assets/isolaser_gtex/cerebellum"
selection <- fread(file.path(A,"selection_counts.tsv"))
points <- fread(file.path(A,"pair_points.tsv"))
gene_points <- fread(file.path(A,"gene_points.tsv"))
point_counts <- fread(file.path(A,"point_counts.tsv"))
variant_matches <- fread(file.path(A,"variant_gene_matches.tsv"))
stats <- fread(file.path(A,"stats.tsv"))
points[, direction_agrees := tolower(as.character(direction_agrees)) == "true"]
fmt <- function(x) format(x,big.mark=",",scientific=FALSE,trim=TRUE)
association_keys <- c("Gene_name","variant_qual","exonic_part")
pair_keys <- c(association_keys,"phenotype_id")
npairs <- uniqueN(points[, ..pair_keys])
nassoc <- uniqueN(points[, ..association_keys])
ngenes <- uniqueN(points$Gene_name)
largest <- stats[view == "All matched pairs" & tp == "6hr" & role == "inclusion"]
hn <- points[gene == "HNRNPK" & tp == "6hr" & variant_qual == "chr9:83980154:C>T"]
sn <- points[gene == "SNHG5" & tp == "6hr"]
variant_label <- function(x) {
  s <- tstrsplit(x,"_",fixed=TRUE)
  paste0(s[[1]],":",s[[2]],":",s[[3]],">",s[[4]])
}
```

We compared our [permutation-adjusted allele-specific splicing results](isolaser_fdr.html)
with significant GTEx v8 **Cerebellum** sQTLs. The tissue is fixed for every
point; there is no selection across tissues. The aim follows the effect-size
comparison in the right panel of
[Fig. 3e of the isoLASER paper](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-64605-6).

**Main finding: `r npairs` distinct matched pairs in `r ngenes` genes**, with
`r nrow(points)` plotted comparisons across baseline, 1 hour and 6 hours.
The genes are **HNRNPK, ATP5MJ, HLA-C and SNHG5**. All comparisons have the
expected effect direction, but there are too few independent genes for a
strong correlation or genome-wide validation conclusion.

# Pair counts and selection

An isoLASER **association** is a gene × variant × exonic part. A **matched
pair** links that association to a GTEx junction for the same variant and
gene. The same pair can be measured at more than one timepoint; a gene can
contribute multiple pairs.

```{r selection_counts}
stage_order <- c("reported","snv","variant_gene","comparable")
flow <- data.table(`Selection step`=c(
  "Reported after permutation FDR and effect screen",
  "Single-base variants eligible for matching",
  "Same variant and gene in GTEx Cerebellum",
  "Comparable annotated splice event"))
for (t in c("0hr","1hr","6hr","any timepoint")) {
  d <- selection[tp == t][match(stage_order,stage)]
  name <- if(t == "any timepoint") "Unique across timepoints" else sub("hr"," hr",t)
  flow[[name]] <- sprintf("%s (%s)",fmt(d$associations),fmt(d$genes))
}
knitr::kable(flow,align="lrrrr")
```

Cells show **isoLASER associations (genes)**. The last column deduplicates
gene–variant–part associations across timepoints; it is not the sum of the
timepoint columns. The input screen requires permutation BH q < 0.05,
isoLASER's `cis` label and |dPSI| ≥ 0.10. BH is performed separately within
each timepoint. Indels are excluded from matching.

The same-variant/gene step contains 30 distinct variant–part associations
from `r uniqueN(variant_matches[,.(Gene_name,variant_qual)])` gene–variant pairs;
one variant can be tested against several parts. The event check leaves
`r nassoc` associations, each with one comparable Cerebellum junction in the
current results, hence `r npairs` distinct matched pairs.

```{r point_counts}
knitr::kable(point_counts[,.(Timepoint=sub("hr"," hr",tp),
  `Inclusion-junction pairs`=inclusion,`Skipping-junction pairs`=skipping,
  `Plotted points`=total,`Distinct genes`=genes)],align="lrrrr")
```

**Five unique pairs give eight timepoint-specific points.** All current
Cerebellum matches are **inclusion junctions**; no skipping-junction match
passes the current filters. These points are not independent signals:
HNRNPK contributes two variants linked to the same part, with measurements
at multiple timepoints.

# How comparable pairs were chosen

**Overlap alone is insufficient.** GTEx tests intron/junction usage, while
isoLASER tests inclusion of an exonic part. We require an annotated local
relationship between the two measurements.

1. **Match variant and gene.** Use the Cerebellum significant-pair file only.
   Require the same GRCh38 position, REF/ALT alleles and Ensembl gene ID.
2. **Check transcript structures.** Use isoLASER's annotation and part
   definitions. Exon-skipping matches require an included transcript with
   both flanking junctions and an excluded transcript with the skipping
   junction. Alternative splice-site matches require junctions sharing one
   endpoint, with the other shifted across the part.
3. **Assign the junction's role.** An inclusion junction occurs in at least
   one part-including transcript and no part-excluding transcript; the
   converse defines a skipping junction. Reject junctions present in both
   groups, and skipping spans containing another non-overlapping annotated
   exon. The junction need not occur in every transcript of its assigned group.
4. **Retain matched pairs.** The primary plot keeps every distinct
   variant–part–GTEx-junction match within Cerebellum, separately at each
   timepoint. It does not reduce the results to one point per gene or select
   a tissue/junction by its p-value. A secondary sensitivity plot selects one
   representative per gene and role using the Cerebellum p-value.

Coordinates are standardized before matching. isoLASER's stored variant
position is 0-based; GTEx variant IDs are 1-based. For example,
`chr9:83980154:C>T` and `chr9_83980155_C_T_b38` identify the same SNP.
The GTEx intron's right endpoint is reduced by one to obtain a 0-based,
half-open interval, following the
[LeafCutter coordinate conversion](https://github.com/davidaknowles/leafcutter/blob/master/clustering/leafcutter_cluster_regtools.py).
Main matches require exact endpoints. The earlier 2-base sensitivity check
did not add any selected matches.

## Example: HNRNPK

![](assets/isolaser_gtex/cerebellum/comparable_event_examples.png)

Gold is the 34-base part chr9:[83980118,83980152); blue is the Cerebellum
GTEx junction chr9:[83978452,83980118), which connects to the part. The
alternative annotated junction ends at 83980152 and excludes it. The diagram
is schematic, not to scale; its coordinates are 0-based.

For the same C>T variant at 6 hours, our ALT-minus-REF inclusion effect is
**`r sprintf("%+.1f",100*hn$dpsi)` percentage points**, and the Cerebellum
inclusion-junction beta is **`r sprintf("%+.2f",hn$slope)`**. Both decrease,
as expected for an inclusion junction.

SNHG5 also has an inclusion-junction match in Cerebellum: dPSI is
`r sprintf("%+.1f",100*sn$dpsi)` points and beta is
`r sprintf("%+.2f",sn$slope)`. These fixed-tissue estimates replace the
different tissue/junction choices in the earlier multi-tissue comparison.

[Download the HNRNPK example as PDF](assets/isolaser_gtex/cerebellum/comparable_event_examples.pdf).

# Effect-size plots

The x-axis is our donor-normalized **ALT minus REF part inclusion**. The
y-axis is GTEx's ALT effect on normalized **intron usage**, from the
[GTEx sQTL pipeline](https://github.com/broadinstitute/gtex-pipeline/blob/master/qtl/leafcutter/README.md).
The axes have different units, so numerical equality is not expected.
Inclusion junctions should have matching effect signs (positive correlation);
skipping junctions would have opposite signs. All matches here are inclusion
junctions, so only those panels are shown.

## What did the paper plot?

The [Fig. 3e caption and methods](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-64605-6.pdf)
describe comparing isoLASER effects with GTEx effects for **matched
variant–splicing associations**, not a gene-level effect summary. A gene may
contribute multiple associations. The linked
[public repository](https://github.com/gxiaolab/isoLASER_paper) contains the
processing workflows; we did not find figure-specific plotting code there,
so its exact duplicate-removal rule remains unverified. Our primary plot
therefore shows matched pairs, with a separate gene-representative sensitivity
view. This is an adaptation of the paper: its displayed example is ovary,
and its described comparison uses the longest skipping junction.

![](assets/isolaser_gtex/cerebellum/cerebellum_gene_effects.png)

## Interpretation

All `r sum(points$direction_agrees)` of `r nrow(points)` comparisons agree
in direction. At 6 hours, Pearson r =
`r sprintf("%.2f",largest$pearson_r)` and Spearman rho =
`r sprintf("%.2f",largest$spearman_rho)`, based on only
**`r largest$points` pairs in `r largest$genes` genes**. These are descriptive
correlations and provide limited external corroboration. They do not
validate the full scan or estimate its FDR. HNRNPK agrees at all three
timepoints; HLA-C still warrants mapping checks.

AHI1, WDR45B and KPNA2 do not enter this comparable-event subset. An absent
match does not disprove an association: we use GTEx significant pairs only,
and adult Cerebellum differs from stimulated hiPSC-derived neurons. The event
check is local and annotation-based; the available files do not establish
the complete structure of every GTEx cluster.

# Matched pairs and data

All rows use **Brain_Cerebellum**. Variant positions are **1-based**, while
part and junction intervals are **0-based, half-open**. dPSI is ALT minus
REF inclusion, shown in percentage points.

```{r matched_pairs}
points[, displayed_variant := variant_label(gtex_variant)]
points[, junction := paste0(sub(":.*","",variant_qual),":",intron_start_0,"-",intron_end_0)]
d <- points[order(gene,tp,variant_qual),.(Gene=gene,Timepoint=sub("hr"," hr",tp),
  `Variant (1-based)`=displayed_variant,`Exonic part (0-based)`=exonic_part,
  `GTEx junction (0-based)`=junction,`Event type`=event_type,
  `Our dPSI (pp)`=round(100*dpsi,1),`Cerebellum beta`=signif(slope,3),
  `GTEx nominal p`=signif(pval_nominal,3),`Our BH q`=signif(q_bh,3))]
DT::datatable(as.data.frame(d),rownames=FALSE,filter="top",extensions="Buttons",
  options=list(pageLength=10,scrollX=TRUE,order=list(),dom="Blfrtip",buttons=c("copy","csv")),
  caption="Eight Cerebellum pair-timepoint comparisons; repeated genes and variants are not independent signals.")
```

Downloads: [all matched pairs](assets/isolaser_gtex/cerebellum/pair_points.tsv),
[selection counts](assets/isolaser_gtex/cerebellum/selection_counts.tsv),
[same-variant/gene matches before the event check](assets/isolaser_gtex/cerebellum/variant_gene_matches.tsv),
[statistics](assets/isolaser_gtex/cerebellum/stats.tsv), and
[input checksums](assets/isolaser_gtex/cerebellum/inputs.tsv).

Reproduce with `Rscript 10.isolaser_permutation/31.cerebellum_comparison.R`,
then `Rscript 10.isolaser_permutation/29.gtex_comparable_examples.R --cerebellum`.
The local output folder is
`10.isolaser_permutation/out/adaptive/gtex_comparison/cerebellum/`.
The earlier multi-tissue outputs remain in its parent folder.
